Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test case sets up a linear optimization with a single variable and a single constraint, then checks the optimal solution found by SimplexSolver.optimize. The current issue report states that recently SimplexTableau had a bug where the detection of basic variables was incorrect: it assumed a nonzero entry in the tableau column indicated a basic variable, but actually the entry must be exactly 1. Checking the SimplexTableau.getBasicRow(int col) method reveals it currently looks for any entry in the column that is not zero (using a tolerance epsilon). If it finds exactly one such entry, it returns its row as the basic variable row, otherwise null. This implies it treats any nonzero tableau entry in that column as basis, contrary to what the bug report describes. This would cause the optimizer to misidentify basic variables, which breaks the simplex computations and could lead to the failed test case not obtaining the correct solution.

Hence, the root cause is the inaccurate implementation of the routine detecting basic variables in the SimplexTableau class. It should require the entry to be 1 (within epsilon), and all other entries in that column should be zero, to satisfy the definition of a basic variable column in a simplex tableau. The previous "last patch" probably introduced this bug because it kept the loose condition of nonzero instead of enforcing equality to 1. This causes the optimization to compute wrong solutions or fail, as shown by the failing test.

The fix should be in SimplexTableau.getBasicRow(int col), adjusting the logic to look for exactly one entry that equals 1 (with tolerance) and ensuring all other entries in the column are zero (with tolerance). This matches the mathematical definition of basic variables in tableau columns. The tested method SimplexSolver.optimize depends on SimplexTableau, so correcting basic variable identification there will fix the test failure.

No relevant clues or conflicting info was found in recent unrelated bug reports, so they can be disregarded.

In summary, the bug is caused by the mis-implementation of basic variable detection in SimplexTableau.getBasicRow which currently accepts any nonzero entry instead of an entry equal to 1, causing failed optimization results in the test.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
